name: Pramila Jayapal
stance: Author of the National AI Charter framework, which would charter AI companies under federal standards that bar the release of risky models, with strict liability and loss of charter for non-compliance; calls for shutting down dangerous models and federal pre-release testing, and criticizes AI-industry election spending against regulation.

statements.text: These AI companies are out of control and a serious threat to our future. We need to shut down their dangerous models and push out the executives who are signing off on their creation.
The majority of Americans see the rapid, unregulated advancement of AI as a serious risk. Congress has to act quickly.
We cannot allow AI to continue to go unregulated and unaccountable.

Congress faces a crossroads — believing AI companies are too big to regulate or question, or requiring them to serve the public and opening the door to real competition. I will be introducing a bill soon to do the latter.
AI companies have the power to shut down their dangerous models, pause development, and stop pouring billions into data centers RIGHT NOW.
Researchers from inside the AI industry are telling us that if we don’t do anything, AI could destroy humanity. Congress needs to act.
Congress must pass AI safety laws and ensure what happened to Sam never happens again.
Republican politicians might claim they now want AI regulation, but last year, they gave billions in tax breaks to some of the very AI companies that are putting our safety at risk.

As demands for AI regulation grow, political groups associated with OpenAI and Anthropic have spent $56 MILLION so far in the 2026 midterms. We cannot let these corporations buy their way out of regulation.
Released the National AI Charter legislative framework, under which AI companies must comply with federal standards that prevent the release of risky models and other serious harms, or be shut down.
My National AI Charter policy changes the entire market structure, forcing AI companies to shut down their dangerous models BEFORE harm occurs.

As long as the damage costs less than the profits, AI companies will keep taking reckless risks. The AI Charter would flip those incentives, holding companies and executives strictly liable for lawbreaking, with loss of charter and criminal penalties for repeat offenders.
We cannot allow AI companies to continue their race to the bottom, leaving our economy, our livelihoods, and our communities to be collateral damage.
It’s about time we hold AI companies accountable before they create harm rather than addressing abuses after the fact.
Congress must also regulate AI just like we have historically done with other emerging industries.
Published an op-ed in The Capitol Forum arguing AI companies should need a federal charter to operate.

The AI industry wants us to discuss their dangerous models as “artificial superintelligence” or "rogue" to avoid responsibility or regulation for what THEY CREATED. We need serious federal testing, just like we test many other products, to ensure AI safety BEFORE harm is done.
Big Tech companies have consolidated the market, making it nearly impossible for more responsible AI models to emerge.
These AI chatbots are prioritizing engagement over safety — and are giving deadly medical advice. This is why we need my AI Charter framework.
Why does Big Tech have so much control? Why aren’t we regulating AI? Follow the money.
